I count the numbers on the street
A key, a map, a borrowed town
The pavement does not know my feet
I learn the bus routes upside down
Nobody knows my name here yet
I'm still a face they have not met
The market opens in the rain
The vendor asks my name again
Maybe someday this will all feel old
It sounds like someone who belongs here
The ferry leaves at half past four
I fold the ticket in my hand
The paint is peeling, line by line
The winter keeps whatever's mine
Time moves slowly in the kitchen
Love is a word I keep misspelling
Home was a porch light left on
I walked the long way round the lake
She wanted rain and got a drought
A little rust along the gate
Every morning starts the same
The fire went out before the dawn
An hour late and nobody cares
I don't remember how we met
You're standing where the river bends
The station clock has stopped at nine
Imagination fills the hall
A precious thing in ordinary hands
The ambitious ones have left the town
Decision made, we drove all night
Conversation drifts across the room
The cathedral bells are ringing twice
I needed you to say my name
We painted every wall and door
Tangled wires behind the old TV
The engine stalled on Tuesday night
Whispered answers to a question nobody asked
Patience is a coin I spend too fast
The radio hums a foreign tune
Collected stamps from places never seen
Hotel soap and paper slippers
Underneath the bridge the water slows
I promised I would call by ten
Our neighbours argue through the wall
Breathe slower, count the ceiling tiles
My brother built a boat from doors
The ocean doesn't care who's right
Serious people never dance alone
Delicious silence after rain
The lonely lighthouse keeper sings
Measure twice, then cut the rope
Children chalked a city on the road
Victory tastes like copper and sleep
Photographs of people I resemble
Remember when the power failed
I wandered through the furniture of strangers
Beautiful mistakes in every line
Electric fences hum at dusk
Nobody answered when I knocked
Little boats returning with the tide
I'd rather wait than guess the answer
Forgotten keys inside a winter coat
Don't mention the weather to my father
Grace is a stranger holding the door
Hollow trees remember every storm
Fire engines passing in the night
Coffee grounds and yesterday's news
Honest mistakes are still mistakes
A thousand reasons and not one excuse
Interesting how the silence grows
A generous hand that never asks for thanks
Curious children chase the cat
I signed the lease and lost the pen
We argued over nothing worth the breath
Twelve hours on a bus with no heat
Loved and wrecked and started over
Mountains look like paper from the plane
Walked in late and nobody turned
Quietly she packed the silverware
Somebody changed the locks last spring
The television talks to empty chairs
Expensive shoes on gravel roads
I tried to leave but left the light on
The orchestra tunes up before the rain
Peculiar habits of the old
Hungry dogs outside the bakery
The universe owes me nothing yet
I wanted proof and got a postcard
Slow applause from an empty hall
Sunday laundry flapping on the line
Gravity wins every argument
Nervous laughter in the waiting room
He carried groceries up nine flights
Somewhere a kettle starts to scream
Wrinkled maps and highlighted routes
Apologies arrive by second post
I counted seventeen red cars
The garden grew without me anyway
A faithful dog and an unfaithful clock
Crossing guards and yellow painted lines
Tired hands that built a thousand chairs
The baker whistles through the flour
Our anniversary fell on a Monday
Glass bottles clinking in the crate
I miss the version of you who laughed
Blue paint beneath the yellow paint
Nobody told the pigeons it was Sunday
We rehearsed goodbye a hundred ways
Wild garlic growing by the tracks
The mechanic shrugged and named a price
Loose change and a folded letter
Thunder over the reservoir
I heard you humming in the other room
Silent partners in a failing shop
Dangerous to wish on Tuesday stars
A borrowed sweater smelling of smoke
The avenue is wider than I thought
Memory is a dog that won't sit
Bicycle bells along the towpath
Volunteers are painting the fence
I never learned to whistle properly
Camera flashes from the balcony
The doctor wrote a word I couldn't read
Daylight leaking through the shutters
Nothing fits inside the suitcase twice
The carpenter measures the doorway
Stolen afternoons beside the canal
I owe the library a fortune
Arrogant and lovely and alone
The scarecrow wears my father's hat
Important letters in a shoebox
Seagulls fight for chips beside the pier
Everything is cheaper after six
Satellite dishes face the same way
She hesitated at the ticket gate
Lovers argue softly in the aisle
Tomorrow's bread is rising in the dark
Visible from the ridge, the tower blinks
I believe the kettle more than the news
Granite steps worn smooth by schoolchildren
The operator says the number's changed
Open windows in November
I read the menu like a letter from you
Celebrate the ordinary Tuesdays
Rusted hinges sing whenever the wind turns
I mapped the cracks across the bathroom tile
Nothing rhymes with what I mean to say
Cardboard boxes labelled later
Mosquitoes hum their only song
The orchard floods in early March
Determined ants rebuild the hill
I washed your cup and left it on the rack
Pianos rot in unheated halls
Monday buried in a pile of post
Wooden spoons and promises to mend
Cigarettes are cheaper by the border
Early frost on purple cabbages
The council cut a ribbon nobody needed
Jealous cousins on a borrowed lawn
Listen for the gate around eleven
Trains run late whenever I am early
Innocent questions cost the most
A paper crown left on the sofa
She counted chickens and came up short
Marigolds wilt against the fence
I photographed the empty chair
Puddles hold the whole grey sky
Tuesday is the loneliest of days
The butcher knows more than he says
Headlights crawl along the valley floor
I planted garlic on your birthday
Envelopes addressed to the previous tenant
Ribbons of fog between the pylons
Nothing here is mine except the view
The lifeguard reads a paperback all day
Reluctant sun above the car park
I sharpened every pencil in the drawer
Cobwebs in the corners of the map
He apologised to the vending machine
Umbrellas bloom at the first drop
The florist sells me something yellow
Half the village waits outside the clinic
Distant sirens stitch the evening shut
I learned your handwriting by heart
Cabbage soup and arguments for dinner
The ferry horn apologises to the fog
Reckless promises beneath the porch
I found a button from your winter coat
Sandwiches sweating in the glovebox
Horizon smudged with someone's bonfire
The widow waters plastic flowers
Thirteen candles on a shop-bought cake
The dentist hums along to something awful
Idle hands and a broken radiator
Everyone pretends to like the soup
Birthday candles sputter in the draught
I returned the ladder but kept the view
Villages go dark at half past ten
The chemist remembers my mother's name
Spare keys under the third pot from the left
Hesitant applause from the back row
Nobody waters the geraniums now
We shared an umbrella and nothing else
The reservoir is lower every summer
Paperwork and pigeons on the ledge
I kept the receipt for the year we lost
Grandmother swore in two languages
Scaffolding hides the cathedral's face
Wet dogs and wool and someone's cigarette
The babysitter fell asleep first
Elderly swimmers at dawn again
I burned the toast and blamed the toaster
The clockmaker's daughter never wears a watch
Bitter oranges along the avenue
Stubborn weeds between the paving stones
I recognised the cough before the face
Nobody claps for the understudy
Cheap wine and expensive opinions
The lamplighter's grandson sells solar panels
Accidental friends from the delayed flight
I hummed the anthem wrong on purpose
The bakery burns the first batch daily
Permission slips and mud on the bus floor
Someone rehearses scales above the launderette
Gentle rain erases yesterday's chalk
The lift is broken; take the stairs
Unopened bills beneath the fruit bowl
I leave the hallway light on for the cat
Velvet seats and bubblegum underneath
He walked the dog and wanted more
You're not the first to miss this turning
Capital letters on the envelope
Dusty trophies for a sport I quit
Imagine every window lit at once
A little fire inside the oil drum
Lately I have been talking to the kettle
Hour by hour the tide forgets the sand
Time and the landlord wait for nobody
Love is the leftover soup reheated
Home is a suitcase that won't close
